A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching v1 Appendices A–C to v2 Appendices B–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic classification experiments and MNIST/CIFAR-10 analyses, including covariance measurements and influence-based training-data removal experiments in Figures 3–7.

after.justification: v2 retains original synthetic and real-data results, revises the MNIST covariance measurements, and adds CIFAR-100 removal-experiment results.

M1.justification: The feature-noise data model, two-layer ReLU CNN, cross-entropy objective, gradient-descent procedure, and influence-score formula in Equation (10) remain unchanged. The additional covariance computation details document the existing approach.

E1.justification: Section 5.2 and Figure 7 add CIFAR-100 to the real-image classification and data-removal experiments. MNIST, CIFAR-10, and the five-class synthetic Gaussian/uniform-noise scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing influence-estimation algorithms. The high-score versus low-score removal comparison is retained; the newly cited implicit-bias studies are not experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 adds ResNet-101 to the evaluation models alongside LeNet and ResNet-18. The synthetic settings, including 100 neurons, learning rate 0.05, and 20 epochs, remain unchanged, as does the removal-fraction evaluation design.

E4.justification: Figure 7 extends the sensitivity analysis comparing removal of high- and low-influence samples to CIFAR-100. This adds evidence for the existing sample-importance question; the synthetic feature-strength, noise-correlation, and dataset-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The theoretical probability bounds are not empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figure 6 substantially replaces the MNIST cross-class numerical evidence: its displayed row-1, column-3 entry changes from -138 to 5607, with widespread off-diagonal revisions and retained diagonal values. Figure 7 also adds CIFAR-100 high/low-removal curves. The principal qualitative conclusions remain.

T1.justification: Condition 3.1(a) adds a covariance-trace requirement involving class sample size. Definition 3.2 replaces the asymptotic long-tail threshold with an explicit inequality, and appendix Equations (132) and (135) revise proof steps. The main theorem's bound forms and most proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The class-dependent-noise mechanism, phase-transition claims, and majority/minority finding retain their meaning. Training-free influence scoring is newly emphasized in the abstract and conclusion, but it was already an explicit contribution in v1.

C2.justification: Remark 3.3 expands v1's brief justification of model-dependent long-tailedness. It explains why classical one-dimensional statistics and sample norms can miss high-dimensional rarity because of concentration, and motivates identifying atypical samples through learned representations.

D1.justification: New Appendix E specifies centered sample covariance with denominator |Si|-1, its eigendecomposition, and reconstruction of Ai for the cross-class norm calculation. v1 only briefly identified sample covariance estimation; the PDFs do not establish whether the underlying implementation changed.

R1.justification: New Appendix A positions the training-dynamics analysis relative to implicit-bias research on flatness, sparsity, margins, and bounded norms. It adds Damian et al. (2021), HaoChen et al. (2021), Soudry et al. (2018), and Xie and Li (2024).

P1.justification: v2 edits terminology and prose, consolidates theorem interpretations, expands the long-tailedness explanation, and adds an Impact Statement and two short appendices. Section-based theorem numbering replaces global numbering, while the main narrative and proof organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains explicit mathematical axis labels; Figures 3–4 use side-by-side panels across the page instead of vertically stacked column panels. Figures 5–7 are resized or restyled, and Figure 7 expands its legend and vertical range for CIFAR-100. The seven-figure organization is retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix E makes the covariance evidence more reproducible, while revised Figure 6 removes negative entries previously presented as squared norms. CIFAR-100 adds support for the influence-score finding, and Remark 3.3 clarifies its conceptual setting. These are useful, bounded gains: the central framework remains largely unchanged, and its theorem now includes an additional applicability condition.
